# How to list the roles, actions, and projects that are yours

This guide shows you how to list the roles you fill, the actions on your plate,
and the projects you are responsible for, optionally filtered by status — all
token-scoped, without naming yourself.

## Prerequisites

- The `glassfrog` CLI installed and on your `PATH`.
- A usable API token stored for the CLI. Each command identifies you by the
  stored token, not by a command-line argument. To store one, run
  `glassfrog auth login` (see `docs/guides/authentication/how-to-store-a-token.md`).

## Steps

### 1. List the roles you fill

```
glassfrog me roles
```

This sends a token-scoped read and prints one block per role — name and id,
then purpose, domains, and accountabilities. When you fill no roles, it prints
exactly `No roles.` and still exits `0`.

### 2. List the actions on your plate

```
glassfrog me actions
```

This prints one entry per action, each with its id, status, description, and
owning role. To narrow to a single status, add `--status`:

```
glassfrog me actions --status current
```

Supported status values: `archived`, `cancelled`, `completed`, `current`,
`scheduled`, `someday`, `waiting`.

### 3. List the projects you're responsible for

```
glassfrog me projects
```

This prints one entry per project, each with its id, status, description, and
owning role (or a `—` marker when no role owns it). The same `--status` filter
applies:

```
glassfrog me projects --status current
```

## Verify

- **Roles:** stdout shows each role as a reshaped projection, and the command
  exits with code `0`. An empty result prints `No roles.` and still exits `0`.
- **Actions:** stdout lists each action with its id, status, description, and
  owning role, and the command exits successfully. No matching actions prints
  the empty-result line `No actions.` and exits successfully.
- **Projects:** stdout lists each project with its id, status, description, and
  owning role, and the command exits successfully. No matching projects prints
  `no projects` and exits successfully.
- **Filtered runs:** with `--status current`, only the items the API returns
  for that status are rendered.
- **Incomplete results:** if more results exist than the first page carried,
  the items you received are printed to stdout and a single note is written to
  **stderr** while the command still exits `0` — so a partial list is never
  silently presented as complete. For `me roles` the note reads:

  ```
  note: more roles exist than shown; pagination is not yet supported, so this list may be incomplete
  ```

  `me actions` and `me projects` signal the same way — a single `note:` line
  on **stderr**, with stdout left as the clean rendered list:

  ```
  note: more actions exist than shown; pagination is not yet supported, so this list may be incomplete
  note: more projects exist than shown; pagination is not yet supported, so this list may be incomplete
  ```

Diagnostics and the incompleteness note always go to **stderr**, never
interleaved into the stdout projection, so stdout pipes cleanly into other
tools.

## Troubleshooting

All failure messages go to **stderr**, name a next step, and never include your
token. The exit code signals the outcome class.

- **"no matching X" is not an error.** An empty list (`No roles.`,
  `No actions.`, `no projects`) is a successful result and exits `0`. If you used
  `--status`, no matches for that status is also a clean empty result — try a
  different status or drop the filter.

- **Not authenticated (no usable token).** stderr reports `not authenticated`
  and points to `glassfrog auth login`; no data is printed and the command
  exits with code `2`. Store a token (`glassfrog auth login` or set
  `GLASSFROG_TOKEN`) and re-run.

- **Unsupported `--status` value.** The command rejects the value before
  issuing any request, naming the unsupported value and listing the supported
  set, and exits with code `2`. Re-run with one of `archived`, `cancelled`,
  `completed`, `current`, `scheduled`, `someday`, `waiting`.

- **Stray argument.** Passing an unexpected positional (for example
  `glassfrog me roles extra-argument`) is rejected as a usage error with no API
  call; the command exits with code `2`. Remove the extra argument.

- **API returned a non-2xx response.** stderr reports that the read failed and
  names the HTTP status; the command exits with code `3`. Check that the token
  has access and retry.

- **API could not be reached** (connection, DNS, TLS, or timeout). stderr names
  the transport failure; the command exits with code `6`. Check network access
  and that the base URL is correct (`--base-url` / `GLASSFROG_BASE_URL` /
  `.glassfrogrc base_url`).
